feature: Feature 2 — Live Swap / Chart / Trade: the coin page, the origin band, and the buy flow

problems.problem: THE ONE RULE IS BREACHED ON THE UNSURE COIN PAGE, AND IT COSTS MONEY. Trace it: story N has two matched mints — $FERRY (verdict=CONFIRMED) and $KANG (verdict=UNSURE). A user pastes the $KANG CA. S3/S4 state 4 QUOTED renders a LIME, ENABLED button labelled `Buy $KANG`; the amber gate (state 9) only fires AFTER the first tap. Meanwhile `.sibstrip` is specified as rendering 'only when story CONFIRMED coin_count ≥2' — coin_count here is 1, so it does not render at all, and it 'only renders for CONFIRMED siblings' so it would never have listed $KANG anyway. Net result: the verified coin from the same story is one row away and is NEVER SHOWN, while a lime Buy sits under a 92px origin band claiming +31m of Insidor lead time that belongs to the story, not to $KANG. This is precisely the ambiguous 'buy which one?' state the ONE RULE says is unrenderable.
problems.fix: Two changes. (1) `.sibstrip` renders at ≥1 CONFIRMED sibling, not ≥2, and when the CURRENT coin's verdict is UNSURE it is promoted out of `.tp2-side` into `.tp2-main` directly beneath the origin band as a 44px cyan band: `The verified coin from this story is $FERRY →`. (2) The resting button label in UNSURE is not `Buy $KANG` in lime — it is amber `.doit` reading `Buy unverified $KANG`, and the two-tap gate morphs it to the acknowledgement copy. A lime button is the terminal's word for 'we stand behind this'; do not spend it on an abstain.

problems.problem: THE MINT-CLOCK GAP REPRODUCES THE EXACT SAFETY.JS DEFECT IN THE EARLINESS LAYER. S2 state 'CONFIRMED, LEAD PENDING' renders `FIRST` / `NOBODY IN CRYPTO HAS POSTED YET` whenever `t_crypto` is null, and explicitly instructs that it 'must read as the best possible news'. But t_crypto = min(t_mint, t_ct) is null both when nobody has posted AND when the PumpPortal websocket is down or the CT poller is stalled. The spec itself defines `mint_stream_gaps` (dataContract item 3) and `story_clocks.gap_window`, then never wires either to this state. Absent is collapsed into best-case — the same `mintAuthority == null ? true : false` logic the spec correctly condemns in api/safety.js line 24, now attached to the product's headline claim.
problems.fix: `FIRST` requires positive evidence of a live clock: render it only when `story_clocks.gap_window = false` AND the PumpPortal sink has a heartbeat within 120s AND the CT poller ran within 4 min. Otherwise the [C] zone renders `—` with sub-label `CLOCK DOWN` and a tooltip naming which sensor is blind. Add a `clock_health` row to the same page query (last heartbeat per sensor) so this is one round trip, not a second fetch.

problems.problem: THE `promoted_at` BACKFILL POLICY IS UNSTATED, AND THE OBVIOUS BACKFILL FABRICATES THE ENTIRE TRACK RECORD. buildOrder step 3 says 'Add `narratives.promoted_at` (set once at PROMOTE, never overwritten)'. Adding a column does not give it to the narratives already in the table. Whoever runs that migration will reach for `created_at` or `first_seen_at` because they are right there — and those timestamps are the ingest/cluster times, not the promote time, which per docs/research/03-system-design.md:50 are separated by the ~8 minute PROMOTE hop plus cluster latency. Backfilling from them inflates every historical lead_time_min by roughly the amount of lead the pipeline actually spends, i.e. it manufactures the number the whole product is sold on.
problems.fix: Write the policy into the migration file, not just the spec: `promoted_at` is NULL for every pre-existing row, NULL propagates to `story_clocks.earliness_eligible = false`, and those stories render `—` / `NOT MEASURABLE` forever. Add a CHECK-style guard in the persist layer (port cluster-persist.js:46-58 verbatim) that refuses any UPDATE where promoted_at is already non-null, and a one-line assertion in the track-record query that excludes `promoted_at IS NULL` rather than coalescing it.

problems.problem: THE AGE CELL AND THE ORIGIN BAND USE TWO DIFFERENT MINT CLOCKS AND WILL VISIBLY CONTRADICT EACH OTHER 150px APART. S1 sources Age from `min(pairCreatedAt) across ALL Solana pairs`. S2's proof line sources `coin minted +2m after spot` from `coin_matches.mint_time`, which comes from `coin_mints.minted_at` (PumpPortal). For a pump.fun coin that graduates, the pumpswap pair's pairCreatedAt is the GRADUATION time, and DexScreener does not reliably keep the original bonding-curve pair in `/latest/dex/tokens/{mint}` afterwards. So the stat grid reads `Age 3h` while the band 34px above it reads `coin minted +2m after spot · 14:04`. The spec introduces `coin_mints` and then does not use it for the one field it is authoritative for.
problems.fix: Age = `coin_mints.minted_at` when present (authoritative), else `min(pairCreatedAt)` across all Solana pairs with a `pool age` micro-label so the weaker source is admitted, else `—`. Never mix: the same timestamp that feeds `delta_minutes` in the origin band must feed the Age cell.

problems.problem: TOP-10 CONCENTRATION IS THE SAME NON-DISCRIMINATING CHECK THE SPEC CORRECTLY KILLS FOR MINT/FREEZE AUTHORITY, AND THE SPEC DOES NOT APPLY ITS OWN RULE. S7 lists `Top 10 holders 68%` as an amber warn row sourced from `/api/holders top10Pct`. On a pre-graduation pump.fun token the bonding-curve PDA holds ~90-99% of supply by construction, so this row renders amber-to-red on literally every genuinely early coin — the exact regime the product exists to serve. The spec suppresses LP-burned for bonding-curve tokens for precisely this reason and then leaves concentration in.
problems.fix: Exclude the bonding-curve PDA, the pool vault, and the burn address from the holder set before computing top10Pct, and derive the percentage over circulating (supply − curve balance) rather than total supply. If the curve address cannot be resolved, suppress the row to a --dim `Top 10 holders — (bonding curve holds most of supply)` rather than showing a number that means nothing. Same rule for `Creator holds 14%`.

problems.problem: `Take back what I put in` IS FALSE BY THE AMOUNT OF THE FEE AND THE PRICE IMPACT — ON THE ONE CONTROL WHOSE ENTIRE VALUE IS THAT ITS LABEL IS LITERALLY TRUE. S5 specifies `qty_to_sell = holdings.cost_basis_usd / current_price_usd`. Selling that quantity returns cost_basis MINUS 0.60% Insidor+Jupiter fee MINUS price impact (which S5 itself says 'bites far sooner' on a thin book) MINUS network fee. On the spec's own $141.20 example that is $2-5 short. The user is told they took back what they put in and did not. Separately, the spec holds both `cost_basis_usd` and `cost_basis_sol` and silently picks USD — so if SOL moved 20% since the buy, 'what I put in' returns a materially different amount of SOL than was spent, with no disclosure of which denomination the promise is in.
problems.fix: Solve for qty against the actual reverse `/order` response, not against spot price: binary-search qty until `outAmount_net_of_feeBps ≥ cost_basis` (2 extra order calls, both already server-side), then clamp to ≤ qty. Label it in the denomination it is computed in: `Take back my $141.20 (after fees)` or `Take back my 0.62 SOL`. State the denomination choice in the spec — USD is right for the normie, SOL is right for the trader, and the Simple/Pro toggle already exists to carry the difference.

problems.problem: SAFETY BLOCKS ARE SPECIFIED ONLY FOR THE BUY DIRECTION, SO THE HONEYPOT CHECK CAN STRAND ITS OWN VICTIMS. S4 state 8 BLOCKED_SAFETY disables `.doit` when B1-B4 fire; S5 says 'All buy-flow states 10-23 apply identically to the sell direction'. State 8 is not in 10-23, so the applicability of B1-B4 to a sell is undefined by omission. If BLOCKED_SAFETY is direction-agnostic, then a user who bought before B3 (transfer hook) was implemented, or before the hook was added by the creator, opens the page and finds Sell disabled by our own safety check — which contradicts the spec's own commitment in S1 TOKEN GONE and S5 DELISTED COIN that we 'never strand a holder'. There is also no state for selling a token WITH a transfer fee: the `.recv` number would overstate proceeds by the fee percentage.
problems.fix: State it explicitly: B1-B4 gate the BUY direction only. The sell direction is never blocked by a safety check — it renders the same `.blockstrip` chrome in amber as a disclosure (`This token charges a 5% transfer fee — you will receive ~5% less than quoted`) and keeps the button live. On sell, subtract `transfer_fee_bps` from the displayed `You receive` and add it as a sixth `.mini` row at equal weight.

problems.problem: INVARIANT (d) — 'a fill is confirmed by getSignatureStatuses, never inferred from a balance change' — HAS NO ROUTE TO CALL. States 16, 22 and 23 all poll `getSignatureStatuses` (at 1s for 45s, and for 90s in AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT). The Helius key lives server-side (api/balance.js holds the RPC plumbing); there is no browser-callable RPC and no `/api/txstatus` in the spec's list of new server routes, which names only `POST /api/order` and `POST /api/execute`. The single most trust-critical invariant in a 23-state machine depends on an endpoint nobody has been told to build.
problems.fix: Add `GET /api/txstatus?sig=` to mechanism A and buildOrder step 6, returning `{confirmationStatus, err, slot}` from a single `getSignatureStatuses` call with `searchTransactionHistory:true`, rate-limited per signature. Specify the poll cadence server-side-friendly (1s for the first 15s, then 3s) so 90s of AMBIGUOUS_TIMEOUT polling from a hundred concurrent users does not exhaust the Helius plan.

problems.problem: THE FEE DOLLAR AMOUNT SILENTLY BECOMES ZERO OR NaN WHEN SOL_PRICE IS UNAVAILABLE, AND THERE IS NO STATE FOR IT. Every dollar figure in the feature — the `.r-fee` value `0.60% · $0.28`, the ⓘ popover's `$0.24 / $0.05 / Total $0.29`, `.recv-usd`, the confirm dialog's `Fees 0.60% · $1.37`, and the Simple-mode risk line `you lose $50` — is computed from `window.SOL_PRICE`, a client global that live.js derives from DexScreener and which is `—` on load and on any DexScreener outage (inventory §1.5 documents the default `—` state). The spec enumerates STALE PIPELINE, NO ROUTE, ABSTAIN and eight other states, and does not enumerate this one. The failure mode is that the mandatory fee disclosure renders `0.60% · $0.00`.
problems.fix: Add SOL_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE as a cross-cutting state: every dollar slot renders `—` (never `$0` — the spec's own semantic rule), the fee row falls back to `0.60% · 0.0026 SOL`, Simple mode's USD-denominated amount field falls back to a SOL field with an amber `.fine` note `Dollar prices unavailable — amounts shown in SOL`, and the risk line falls back to `If this goes to zero you lose 0.22 SOL.` Move the SOL price to the server response of `/api/order` so the fee disclosure never depends on a browser global at all.

problems.problem: THE SIBLING QUERY REFERENCES A COLUMN THE SPEC'S OWN DDL DOES NOT DEFINE. dataContract KEY QUERY SHAPES orders the `.sibstrip` by `cm.score desc, cm.mint_time asc, t.liquidity desc`, but dataContract item 9 defines `tokens` as `(mint pk, ticker, name, decimals, token_program, logo_url, pair_address, first_pair_created_at, socials jsonb, updated_at)` — there is no `liquidity`. Market data is explicitly described as living on DexScreener and being fetched per-request via /api/token-lookup. The query does not compile, and the tiebreak it encodes (prefer the deeper book) cannot be evaluated in SQL at all.
problems.fix: Either add `liquidity_usd numeric, liquidity_updated_at timestamptz` to `tokens` written by a periodic refresher (and accept it is minutes stale, which is fine for a tiebreak), or drop the third sort key and resolve ties client-side after the /api/token-lookup batch returns. Say which. The same gap applies to the `.sibstrip` row content — it shows `mcap · age`, neither of which is in the tokens DDL either.

problems.problem: NOTHING ADDRESSES SUPABASE RLS AGAINST PRIVY IDENTITY, WHICH GATES holdings, trades AND THE ENTIRE REALTIME SECTION. Mechanism J correctly identifies the Privy-token-expiry-kills-Realtime bug and calls it 'the most likely launch-day bug'. The larger one is upstream: `holdings` and `trades` are keyed on `user_id` and hold a user's cost basis, PnL, wallet and fee history. Supabase RLS evaluates `auth.uid()` from a Supabase-issued JWT; Privy issues its own. Without a custom JWT signing key configured on the Supabase project and a claim mapping, either RLS is off (every user can read every other user's positions and our entire fee-revenue ledger) or `setAuth()` has nothing meaningful to authorise. Realtime on `coin_matches` additionally requires the table to be added to the `supabase_realtime` publication, which is not mentioned anywhere.
problems.fix: Add to buildOrder step 6, before holdings ship: configure Privy as a third-party JWT issuer on Supabase, map `sub` → the `user_id` used by holdings/trades, write RLS policies (`user_id = auth.jwt()->>'sub'`) on both tables, and add `alter publication supabase_realtime add table coin_matches, story_clocks`. Note that `coin_matches` and `story_clocks` are public-read (they are page content) while holdings/trades are owner-read — two different policy shapes.

problems.problem: THE ONRAMP RETURN CONTRACT RESTORES THE INTENT BUT NOT THE PRICE, WHICH MAKES THE NORMIE'S FIRST TRADE THE WORST ONE. S6 persists `insidor.pending_buy = {mint, side, amountSol, slippageBps, priorityTier, ts}` and returns the user to a 44px cyan band: `Money ready — $47.30 of SOL landed. Continue your buy?`. The spec's own mechanism I concedes settlement takes 30s–15min. On a coin that is 20 minutes old, 15 minutes is the entire move. The band offers `Continue` against a quote that is between one and forty-five TTLs stale, and the state machine has no transition covering 'pending intent resurrected against a materially different market'.
problems.fix: The return band never offers a bare `Continue`. On rehydration, immediately re-order and render a comparison at equal typographic weight: `When you left, $47.30 bought 231,402 FERRY. It now buys 96,110 (−58%).` with `Buy anyway` and `Change amount`. Add the state as `24 INTENT_RESUMED_PRICE_MOVED` and require an explicit tap when |Δ outAmount| > 5%, reusing the amber `flashDn` treatment already specified for the 1% in-panel case.

problems.problem: MULTI-WALLET USERS COLLAPSE INTO ONE holdings ROW AND CORRUPT BOTH COST BASIS AND minutes_early. `holdings` is specified `unique on (user_id, mint)` while carrying a `wallet` column, and `.poscard` reads on-chain qty from `/api/balance?owner=&mint=`. Privy routinely gives a user an embedded wallet plus a linked external wallet. Buy on the embedded wallet, connect Phantom, and the page compares Phantom's qty against a row whose cost basis came from a different wallet — which trips the spec's own `>0.5% mismatch` rule into COST BASIS STALE for a position that is perfectly well understood. Worse, the frozen `minutes_early_when_bought` on that row is now displayed against a holding it does not describe.
problems.fix: Make the uniqueness `(user_id, wallet, mint)` and render `.poscard` for the active wallet only, with a `2 wallets hold this` chip linking to a combined view. Aggregate across wallets only in the `What you own` list, where each row names its wallet. The frozen earliness number belongs to the wallet-scoped row, not the user.

problems.problem: THE LEAD NUMERAL IS A MONUMENT, NOT A CLOCK — WHICH IS THE THESIS MISS. `+31m EARLY VS CRYPTO` is `t_crypto − promoted_at`: a historical fact about a race that is already over. What a trader standing on this page at 14:40 needs to know is how much of that lead is still unspent — the story promoted at 14:02, crypto picked it up at 14:33, so his personal lead is now −7m and falling, and the page happily shows him a big cyan `+31m` next to a Buy button. The product's own D2/honest-record instinct is applied to the story's record and not to the user's live position in the race. This is the one place where the page reads like it is selling the pipeline rather than serving the trader.
problems.fix: [C] gets a second line under the numeral, mono 10.5px: while `t_crypto` is null, `your lead right now +18m` counting DOWN live from `promoted_at + elapsed`; once t_crypto lands, `crypto caught up 7m ago` in amber, then red past 30m. The frozen `+31m` stays as Insidor's record; the live line is the user's. They are different numbers and the spec already establishes exactly this distinction for `.poscard` (`minutes_early_when_bought` vs story lead) — apply the same discipline here.

problems.problem: THE ORIGIN BAND IS A CONSUMER HERO CARD IN A SCREENER, AND THE SIBLING STRIP IS BELOW THE FOLD. The band is 92px tall with a 56px thumb, three stacked lines, a 172px right zone and a 96px CTA — 32% taller than the settled `.tp-origin` (48px thumb, two lines, ~70px) and the largest element on the page after the chart. The terminal's own vocabulary for 'story plus numbers' is a ranked row: `.tnr` at 54px min-height, 42px thumb, min-width:0 title cell, right-aligned mono columns. Separately, `.tp2-side` stacks poscard(168) + tradebox(470) + secbox(180) + sibstrip(44+) ≥ 862px inside a `position:sticky` column; on a 1080p display (~940px usable) a holder's `.sibstrip` sits permanently below the fold and the bottom of `.secbox` is marginal. The two surfaces that carry the moat are the tall one nobody scrolls past and the short one nobody scrolls to.
problems.fix: Rebuild the band on the `.tnr` grid: `42px thumb | minmax(0,1.9fr) title+snippet | 92px SPOTTED | 92px CRYPTO | 108px LEAD | 76px matched-chip`, header hairlines and right-aligned mono values, 58-62px tall. Same facts, terminal grammar, 30px given back. Move `.sibstrip` out of `.tp2-side` and into `.tp2-main` directly under the band — it is story information, not trade information, and it belongs beside the earliness claim it qualifies.

problems.problem: THE FIRST-RUN PANEL REPLACES THE TRADEBOX BODY, WHICH IS WHERE `.blockstrip` LIVES. S6 specifies `.firstrun` as replacing the `.tradebox` body in place with three friendly steps and a `Start with $50` button. S4 specifies `.blockstrip` as a 34px red strip 'directly above the buy button' inside that same body, justified by 'a user must never have to scroll to a side panel to learn why the button is dead'. Compose them: a brand-new user lands on a token where B4 (no sell route — the honeypot signature) has fired, and sees a warm three-step explainer ending in `Start with $50`. The one user who cannot evaluate the risk is the one user shown none of it.
problems.fix: `.firstrun` never renders over a BLOCKED_SAFETY state. Add FIRSTRUN_BLOCKED: the explainer collapses to one line (`We block buying on this coin — see why below`) above a full-weight `.blockstrip`, and the primary becomes a ghost `Find a safer coin →` to the trending queue. Also define precedence explicitly for firstrun × UNVERIFIED_MATCH_GATE × CHECKS PENDING, all three of which target the same 470px of panel.

problems.problem: WITH TWO CONFIRMED STORIES, THE LEAD NUMERAL IS CHOSEN BY MATCH SCORE — i.e. BY THE NUMBER MOST LIKELY TO FLATTER. S2's MULTIPLE CONFIRMED STORIES state 'shows the highest-scoring story and appends `also matched to 1 other story →`'. Match score measures how confident we are that this coin came from that story; it says nothing about which story is the earlier or truer origin. If story A (score .91, promoted 14:02, lead +31m) and story B (score .88, promoted 13:10, lead +4m) both confirm, we display +31m — the larger claim, selected by a criterion unrelated to earliness. Nothing in the UI reveals that a competing confirmed origin implies a smaller lead.
problems.fix: When two CONFIRMED stories exist and their `lead_time_min` differ by more than 10 minutes, render the SMALLER lead (the conservative claim) and change the appendix to `also matched to Bergen Horn (+31m) →`, so the bigger number is reachable but not the headline. When they agree within 10 minutes, keep the higher-scoring story's copy.

problems.problem: THE `first` BADGE IN `.sibstrip` ENDORSES THE SNIPER COIN. Rows are ordered `score desc, mint_time asc, liquidity desc` with 'the earliest-minted badged `first`'. On a story that mints five coins in ninety seconds, the earliest is very often a bot deploy with $200 of liquidity and one holder, and the community coin is third. `first` is the only word on that strip that looks like a verdict, and it points at the coin most likely to be a trap — on a page whose whole premise is that being first is good.
problems.fix: Rename the badge to `earliest` (a fact, not a verdict) in --dim rather than cyan, and add a second badge `deepest` in cyan on the highest-liquidity row. Two neutral facts beat one word that reads as a recommendation.

problems.problem: NOTHING ON THE PAGE ROUTES TO THE TRACK RECORD, SO THE +31m IS A CLAIM RATHER THAN A RECORD. D2 commits to misses visible by default with an `All` filter, and S2 correctly ships negative leads in red. But the coin page — the only surface where the earliness claim is adjacent to a spend decision — offers no path to the aggregate. A sceptic can check one permalink and one clock; they cannot see that roughly a third of detections are late, which the founder decisions treat as a feature.
problems.fix: One 11.5px mono line in the origin band footer or the Info pane, sourced from the same story_clocks aggregate that powers the record: `Insidor was late on 31% of the last 200 detections — see the record →`. It costs one cached count and converts the numeral from marketing into evidence.

problems.problem: THE EXECUTE-TIME FEE RECONCILIATION CHECKS A FIELD THAT PROBABLY DOES NOT EXIST. Mechanism B: 'If the fee in the execute-time response differs from the displayed fee by more than 2 bps, abort to CONFIRM_EXPIRED and re-render.' But the fee is baked into the transaction assembled at `/order`; `/execute` is specified in the spec's own route contract as returning `{status, signature, error, code, slot}` — no fee field. The reconciliation as written can never fire, which means the guarantee 'the disclosed number and the charged number must be the same number' is unenforced.
problems.fix: Reconcile at the right seam: freeze `feeBps` + `platformFee.feeBps` from the `/order` response that produced the signed transaction, and re-assert equality against the SAME requestId's order record server-side inside `/api/execute` before forwarding. Since requestId is single-use, the transaction that gets submitted is by construction the one whose fee was displayed — say that, and drop the phantom execute-time comparison. Additionally verify the actual fee post-fill from the parsed transaction and write it to `trades.fee_bps_charged`, so a divergence is at least detectable after the fact.

problems.problem: FAILED_SLIPPAGE AND FAILED_EXPIRED_BLOCKHASH WITHHOLD THE SIGNATURE THEY ACTUALLY HAVE. State 21 FAILED_ONCHAIN is described as 'the one failure where a transaction exists' and is the only state given a Solscan link. That is wrong for 18: a Jupiter 6001 / SlippageToleranceExceeded is an on-chain revert — the transaction landed, consumed a fee, and is on the explorer. State 19's expired blockhash may also have a signature that simply never confirmed. The spec's own honesty standard ('tell them exactly what happened to their money') is met everywhere except the two most common failures.
problems.fix: Render the signature and Solscan link in 18 and 19 whenever one exists, alongside the existing copy. Same `.ca-box` treatment as the `.done` state (§9.4), so the component is already built.

problems.problem: COST BASIS IS COMPUTED FROM A CLIENT-SIDE PRICE GLOBAL. `holdings.cost_basis_usd` / `avg_price_usd` / `realised_pnl_usd` and `trades.usd_at_trade` all require a USD price at fill time, and the only USD source named anywhere in the feature is `window.SOL_PRICE` (live.js, `insidor-sol-price` event). A browser global is trivially manipulable, unavailable when DexScreener is down, and differs between two of the user's own devices. It becomes the denominator of every PnL number, the `Take back what I put in` quantity, and the realised/unrealised split.
problems.fix: Capture the SOL/USD price server-side inside `/api/execute` at submission and persist it on the `trades` row (`sol_usd_at_trade`); derive `usd_at_trade` and cost basis from that column only. The client global stays for display of live prices and for nothing that is written to the database.

missing: SOL_PRICE UNAVAILABLE — enumerated nowhere despite every dollar figure on the page, including both mandatory fee disclosures, depending on it.

REJECTED MATCH — the page query filters `verdict in ('CONFIRMED','UNSURE')`, so a coin whose match was matched-then-REJECTED renders identically to a coin that was never matched at all. A user who bookmarked or was sent the link when it was CONFIRMED gets a silent disappearance. S8 covers CONFIRMED→UNSURE while held but not →REJECTED, which is the more serious withdrawal.

DECIMALS UNKNOWN — `You receive = order.outAmount / 10^decimals`. On a 40-second-old mint not yet in `tokens`, decimals is null and the headline receive figure is wrong by a power of ten. No state prevents rendering it; the spec should pin QUOTING until getAccountInfo returns an authoritative decimals.

SELL CONFIRM DIALOG — S5 says buy states 10–23 apply identically, but the six confirm rows are buy-shaped. A seller needs a 7th row (`This sale realises +$38.40`), and `Amount`/`You receive` need to swap denominations. Currently unspecified.

SELL OF A TRANSFER-FEE / TRANSFER-HOOK TOKEN — B3 blocks the buy; nothing describes the holder who already owns one, whose `You receive` is overstated by the fee and whose transaction may be arbitrarily rejected by the hook.

TWO-TAP GATE EXPIRY DURING CONFIRM — the gate times out after 4s, but state 10 CONFIRM can sit open for 20s+ and CONFIRM_EXPIRED can extend it indefinitely. Whether the acknowledgement survives a refresh-quote cycle is undefined.

PRIORITY BUMP FROM THE TOP TIER — state 19 'auto-bumps the priority tier one level' but the tiers are exactly two (Fast, Turbo). Retrying a Turbo failure has nowhere to go and the spec does not say what happens.

MULTIPLE PENDING INTENTS / STALE pending_intent — `insidor.pending_buy` is a single localStorage slot. Starting a funding flow on coin A, abandoning it, then funding for coin B leaves a stale intent whose TTL and eviction rule are unspecified, and the return band could fire on the wrong mint.

CONCURRENT TABS — the same requestId or two simultaneous buys of the same mint from two tabs. `trades.request_id unique` catches the second submission at the DB, but the spec never says when the row is inserted (at ORDERING or at SUBMITTING), which decides whether the invariant actually holds.

FIRST-RUN × EVERY OTHER PANEL STATE — `.firstrun` replaces the tradebox body, colliding with `.blockstrip` (BLOCKED_SAFETY), the two-tap gate (UNVERIFIED), CHECKS PENDING, and NO ROUTE. Precedence is undefined for all four.
MINT-CLOCK GAP AS A PAGE-LEVEL STATE — `mint_stream_gaps` and `story_clocks.gap_window` are defined in the data contract and never surfaced in any of S2's eight states.

EMPTY `What you own` — S8 specifies HELD, DUST, CLOSED and four earliness variants but never the zero-position case, which is what every new user sees and which is the natural home for the first-run explainer's entry point.
